entries.proposition: System: eight-week-old male C57BL/6 wild-type mice, chronic PTZ kindling, a PTZ-induced acquired epilepsy model.
entries.snippet: Eight-week-old male C57BL/6 mice, weighing 20.1 ± 2.3 g

entries.proposition: Group size: 16 per group for behaviour; molecular readouts are n = 3 and mitochondria n = 5.
entries.snippet: the mice were randomly assigned into four groups (n = 16 per group)

entries.proposition: Text asserts reduced kindling success rate and seizure duration and longer latencies with PX-478.
entries.snippet: the seizure scores, full kindling success rates, and seizure duration after the final injection were significantly reduced in the PTZ + PX-478 group

entries.proposition: Table 2, PTZ + PX-478 row: 56.3 percent kindled, kindling latency 19.11 +- 1.05 d, seizure latency 215.56 +- 9.86 s, duration 48.56 +- 4.72 s (the PTZ row reads 75.0 percent, 16.00 +- 1.21, 206.00 +- 10.92, 62.15 +- 3.39).

Figure 2 (seizure score per PTZ injection, n = 16): the PTZ and PTZ + PX-478 curves separate from about injection 3, with asterisks on several injections, reaching about 4.7 against about 4.1 at the last injections; control curves at 0.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2: line chart seizure score 0 to 5 against PTZ injection times 1 to 11, PTZ curve rising to about 4.7, PTZ plus PX-478 curve to about 4.1, CON and CON plus PX-478 flat at 0, asterisks at injections 3 to 11.

entries.proposition: Statistics text for blots and assays: each measurement repeated at least three times, group n of 3 in the figures.
entries.snippet: Each behavioral testing and molecular biology experiment was repeated at least three times.

entries.proposition: ROS by DHE: described as 'appeared to have higher' ROS in PTZ; the Methods describe ImageJ quantification of ROS fluorescence.
entries.snippet: the PTZ group appeared to have higher ROS levels in hippocampal CA1, CA3, and DG tissues

entries.proposition: Figure 4A shows DHE and DAPI micrographs for CA1, CA3 and DG in four groups with faint red signal in PTZ; Figure 4B and C plot SOD, CAT, GSH-Px and MDA as bar charts of n = 3, but no bar chart quantifies the DHE fluorescence.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 4A: grid of ROS, DAPI and merge panels for CA1, CA3 and DG across CON, PTZ, PTZ+PX-478 and CON+PX-478, red signal visible but faint in PTZ; panels B and C: bar charts of relative SOD, CAT and GSH-Px activity and relative MDA, three points per bar; no DHE intensity chart.

experimental_context.treatment: PTZ 35 mg/kg every other day, with or without PX-478 5 mg/kg

entries.qualifies_needle: appeared to have higher ROS levels

entries.proposition: Figure 3 H&E panels (CA1, CA3, DG; four groups) are single low-power fields at 100 um scale bars with no neuronal count or damage score; differences are subtle at the deposited resolution.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3: 3 by 4 grid of H and E sections, CA1, CA3 and DG rows, CON, PTZ, PTZ+PX-478, CON+PX-478 columns, pyramidal layers visible with scale bars; no quantification chart.

entries.proposition: Text on ferroptosis markers lists GPX4 among markers elevated in PTZ and decreased by PX-478.
entries.snippet: GPX4, prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2)/cyclooxygenase 2 (COX-2), ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH-1), and transferrin (TRF) were significantly elevated in the PTZ group compared with those in the CON and CON + PX-478 groups

experimental_context.treatment: PTZ 35 mg/kg every other day, with or without PX-478 5 mg/kg

entries.proposition: Figure 6B (GPX4): in PTZ the GPX4 mRNA bar is about 0.45 and the protein bar about 0.3 of control, with a weaker GPX4 band, and PX-478 restores both to about 0.9 and 0.8; GPX4 is therefore LOWER in PTZ, not elevated, unlike PTGS2, FTH-1 and TRF in panels C and D.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 6B: three panels, relative GPX4 mRNA expression (CON 1.0, PTZ about 0.45, PTZ+PX-478 about 0.9, CON+PX-478 about 1.0), relative GPX4 protein expression (about 1.0, 0.3, 0.8, 1.05) and a GPX4 over beta-actin blot with a weaker PTZ lane.

experimental_context.treatment: PTZ 35 mg/kg every other day, with or without PX-478 5 mg/kg

entries.proposition: Discussion states GPX4 activity falls during ferroptosis, which fits the panel and not the Results sentence.
entries.snippet: Intracellular antioxidants such as GSH are depleted, the cystine/glutamate antiporter system is downregulated, and GPX4 activity is reduced during ferroptosis.

entries.proposition: Figure 5 TEM: mitochondria are smaller with denser matrix in PTZ; length about 0.65 against about 1.15 um in control and about 0.8 in PTZ + PX-478; n = 5 per the legend, with no statement whether n counts mice or mitochondria.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 5A-B: TEM at 5.0 um, 2.0 um and 500 nm scales across four groups with red arrows on mitochondria; bar charts of mitochondrial length (about 1.15, 0.65, 0.82, 1.13 um) and area (about 0.35, 0.17, 0.26, 0.35 um2) with asterisks.

entries.proposition: Ferroptosis is inferred from MDA, Fe2+ and marker expression and mitochondrial morphology; no ferroptosis inhibitor, lipid peroxide probe or cell-death assay is used.
entries.snippet: This result indicates that epilepsy leads to ferroptosis damage, and that PX-478 injection helps inhibit ferroptosis occurrence.

entries.proposition: The paper presents PX-478 as BBB-permeant and low in oral toxicity, a claim supported by citation only.
entries.snippet: Notably, unlike other HIF-1α inhibitors, PX-478 exhibits low oral toxicity and can penetrate the blood–brain barrier, making it more suitable for therapeutic use

entries.proposition: Stated limits: species and an 'acute' focus; no long-term or adverse outcome.
entries.snippet: this study primarily focused on the acute effects of PX-478 treatment and did not extensively explore its long-term impacts and potential adverse outcomes
